proteins.note: The pII protein binds to the intergenic region in double-stranded, supercoiled DNA (replicative form) and nicks the positive strand. The resulting free 3' OH terminus serves as a primer for new strand synthesis using host factors (Rep helicase, DNA polymerase III). After a full round of replication, pII circularizes the displaced DNA strand. Newly synthesized (+) single stranded DNA is either converted to RF DNA or packaged as genomes, depending on the concentrations of ssDNA binding protein pV and a separately expressed fragment of pII termed pX. Functions: DNA replication initiation

proteins.note: Minor coat protein pIII is located at the tail of the filamentous phage particle. It is involved in termination of assembly and infectivity. In the absence of pIII abnormally long phage particles are formed and remain attached to host cells. In addition, pIII is involved in initiating infection of host cells by binding to pili. In the case of the Ff phages, pIII binds to the tip of F-pili and then interacts with the TolA protein. The assembly termination function maps to the C-terminus of pIII, whereas the receptor binding maps to the N-terminus. Ike and f1 proteins cannot replace one another. Functions: receptor binding, morphogenesis, structural.

The pVI proteins of Ff phages are minor coat proteins that are located at the end of the virion. They are involved in termination of assembly. In the absence of pVI, phage particles remain associated with the host membrane.

proteins.note: The pI protein of filamentous phages is involved in morphogenesis and may hydrolyze ATP. It is an inner membrane protein and interacts with the outer membrane protein pIV. The N-termini of members of this cluster share homology to the zonular occludens toxin (Zot) encoded by phage CTXphi. However, the toxin activity of Zot was mapped to the C terminus, which is divergent in the proteins in this cluster. pXI is the product of translational reinitiationin gene I and interacts with pI.
